title: CIA Agents in Mexico Were Elite: Green Berets, Counterterrorists, Tested in Afghanistan
author: SinEmbargo Staff
content:
_This article by[SinEmbargo
Staff](https://www.sinembargo.mx/author/redaccion/) originally appeared in the
[October 20, 2026 edition of
SinEmbargo](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4890600/agentes-de-cia-eran-de-elite-
boinas-verdes-antiterroristas-probados-en-afganistan/), an independent Mexican
digital news outlet._

**Mexico City, October 20 (SinEmbargo).–** Before arriving in Chihuahua, where
they took part in state operations without authorization from the Government
of Mexico, [CIA agents](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4890202/los-agentes-muertos-
de-la-cia-ya-operaban-en-chihuahua-desde-2025-revela-fiscalia/) **Richard
Leiter Johnston III and John Dudley Black** served in the **United States
Armed Forces** and took part in missions in **Afghanistan**. One belonged to
the U.S. Army Special Forces and the other served in the Marine Corps. Their
military careers took them from these war zones to the illegal covert
operation on Mexican territory that came to light when both died, on April 19,
2026, in a rollover in the **Sierra Tarahumara**.

The Americans were not mere drone-operation instructors, as the Chihuahua
Attorney General's Office, then headed by **César Jáuregui Moreno** ,
initially maintained. According to the investigation of the **Federal Attorney
General 's Office** (FGR), presented at last weekend's hearing, the two agents
took part, armed, in the deployment, supposedly against clandestine synthetic
drug laboratories in the community of El Pinal. Their presence in the state
was not limited to the days before their deaths; the documentation presented
by the Public Prosecutor's Office during the hearing against Jáuregui
indicates that they had been in Chihuahua since at least October 2025.

The Public Prosecutor's Office also revealed that Richard Leiter Johnston was
in Chihuahua from October 2025 and returned from January 21 to 31, 2026. He
also had a reservation from April 14 to 20, the period in which he took part
in the operation. For his part, John Dudley Black, the other American who
died, was staying in room 2312 of the Holiday Inn hotel, where his belongings
remained. The Prosecutor's Office also documented that Johnston rented two
gray Volkswagen Jetta vehicles from the company Eurocar, under contracts 81957
and 85272.

A report prepared on May 15, 2026, based on the GPS records of both vehicles,
revealed that they remained for long periods at the State Public Security
Complex, particularly near the C4 Office of Strategic Operations. For the
Public Prosecutor's Office, these movements made it possible to establish a
relationship between the Americans and the state security facilities. The
information matched the testimony of an agent who stated that, on April 16, he
had seen an unofficial gray car driven by a man he identified as apparently
American in the Strategic Operations parking lot.

## A Green Beret With Missions in Afghanistan and the Philippines

Richard Leiter Johnston III served as a platoon leader in the 25th Infantry
Division, where he led soldiers in support of Operation Freedom Sentinel in
Afghanistan in 2016, carrying out counterterrorism operations and training the
Afghan Security Forces, according to his obituary published by Murphy Funeral
Homes, which states that he “died on April 19, 2026 while serving his country
overseas.” His story was also published on _U.S. Special Forces Taps_ , a site
dedicated to veterans of U.S. special operations.

Johnston continued his military training until he joined the U.S. Army Special
Forces. He passed the selection and qualification course that allowed him to
earn the Green Beret, the insignia of the units specialized in unconventional
operations. He also received training in combat, airborne operations, military
free fall, and combat diving. According to his obituary, he went on to command
Special Forces Operational Detachment SFOD-A 1333, with which he took part in
joint military exercises in Southeast Asia and was deployed to the Philippines
to work with local forces in operations against terrorist organizations.

![Richard Leiter Johnston III](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/10/cia-agents-elite-green-berets-
afghanistan-02.jpg)Richard Leiter Johnston III, a former member of the U.S.
Army Green Berets and CIA agent, took part in counterterrorism missions in
Afghanistan and the Philippines before operating in Chihuahua, where he died
on April 19, 2026. Photo: SinEmbargo

After leaving the Army, Richard was selected to work in the Middle East,
Africa, East Asia, and the Western Hemisphere. Throughout his career, Richard
used his command of Mandarin and his self-taught Spanish to operate better in
these regions, according to his obituary, which omits any explicit mention of
the CIA and does not identify Chihuahua as the place of his death.

> “Richard's life was tragically cut short in a traffic accident while
> carrying out his duty, supporting our country's priorities. His tireless
> dedication, committed to fulfilling the mission until the very last moment,
> is a testament to his devotion. He was doing work he firmly believed in,
> using the skills he had honed throughout his career,” reads the same
> obituary.

## John Dudley Black: From the Marines to the Sierra Tarahumara

John Dudley Black, the other American who died in Chihuahua, also had a
military career that included Afghanistan. He was born in San Francisco,
California, but grew up in Spokane, Washington, where he studied at Trinity
Catholic School and then at Gonzaga Preparatory School, from which he
graduated in 2001.

During his school years he played football and ran track. He later enrolled at
Gonzaga University and took part in its reserve officer training program
before joining the Marine Corps, journalist Alexandra Duggan reported in a
story published by _The Spokesman-Review_ and later picked up by _The Seattle
Times._

Duggan maintains that text messages sent to friends announcing Black's death
indicate that he took part in the university's Reserve Officers' Training
Corps. He also served in Afghanistan, according to the same report. The
profile also highlights how, in a 2013 video published on the official website
of the U.S. Marine Corps, Black spoke of his experience in Afghanistan as
aide-de-camp to the commanding general of the 1st Marine Division.

The careers of Johnston and Black took on another dimension when Mexican
authorities began to reconstruct their movements in Chihuahua. The data
presented during the arraignment hearing against César Jáuregui revealed that
the Americans' presence went back to at least October 2025. The state Public
Prosecutor's Office presented hotel reservations, vehicle rental contracts,
and geolocation records that made it possible to identify their movements, as
well as **prolonged stays at public security facilities**.

![John D. Black](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/cia-
agents-elite-green-berets-afghanistan-03.jpg)John D. Black, a former member of
the U.S. Marine Corps and CIA agent, served in Afghanistan before taking part
in security operations in Chihuahua, where he died in a rollover on April 19,
2026. Photo: SinEmbargo

The investigation also shed light on the role Johnston and Black played in the
last days of their lives. According to testimony gathered by Mexican
authorities, both were in contact with Guillermo Arturo Zuany Portillo, then
Special Prosecutor for Strategic Operations and Anti-Kidnapping, who allegedly
coordinated the presence of the U.S. personnel. Those testifying said the
foreigners received rifles in Zuany's office before heading to El Pinal, in
the Sierra Tarahumara, on April 16.

Details of their operation published by _El Universal_ describe much more
direct participation. According to those reports, Johnston and Black were part
of the tactical group, carried rifles and balaclavas, checked coordinates on
electronic tablets, and coordinated with the director of the State
Investigation Agency, Pedro Román Oseguera Cervantes. These elements contrast
with the initial version of the Chihuahua authorities, who presented the
Americans as instructors from the United States Embassy who had only asked to
travel with state officials.

Between April 17 and 19, the deployment of Mexican authorities supposedly
focused on destroying facilities supposedly used to produce synthetic drugs
near El Pinal, in the municipality of Morelos. Returning from the operation,
in the early hours of April 19, a pickup truck that was part of the convoy
fell into a ravine near the community of Polanco and caught fire. Johnston and
Black were traveling in the vehicle, along with Pedro Román Oseguera Cervantes
and his bodyguard, Manuel Genaro Méndez Montes. All four died. The accident
exposed a collaboration that, according to the investigations, **had not been
authorized by the Mexican federal government**.

The controversy deepened when the FGR began reviewing the circumstances of the
operation and the first explanations offered by state authorities. According
to reports by _El País_ , investigators reviewed security cameras at the
Prosecutor's Office facilities and interviewed members of the operation. One
of the witnesses said that, after the accident, he received instructions to
conceal the presence of CIA personnel. The same report indicates that the
pickup was carrying extra fuel in jerry cans, a circumstance that the
testimonies linked to the fire after the fall.
